notes: Reigned as king of Goguryeo from 391 until 413 and led major territorial expansion across Manchuria and the Korean Peninsula.

Represents Liu Bei's territorial regime from his entry into Yi Province in 211 through the formal establishment of Shu Han in 221 and his imperial reign until 223. Shu Han is used as the map-level polity label for the wider Liu Bei faction.

Represents Zhuge Liang's service to the Liu Bei faction from the Yi Province campaign in 211 through the establishment of Shu Han and his later service as chancellor and regent until 234. Shu Han is used as the map-level polity label for the wider faction.

role: General and governor of Jing Province
notes: Served as a leading general of Liu Bei's faction from the Yi Province campaign period until his defeat and death in 220. Although he died before the formal proclamation of Shu Han in 221, Shu Han is used as the map-level polity label for the wider Liu Bei faction.
Liu Bang reigned as the founding emperor of the Han dynasty from 202 to 195 BCE. The polity is labeled Western Han for map-level distinction from Eastern Han.
Became active in the British women's suffrage movement after 1907 and remained engaged in public and charitable work until her death in 1948.

role: Head of State and Supreme Commander
notes: Led the Provisional Government of Free India and the Indian National Army from 1943 until 1945.
Conventionally dated as king of the united Kingdom of Israel from about 970 to 931 BCE; the chronology is traditional and debated.
Active as a leading Neoplatonist teacher and scholar in Alexandria from the late fourth century until her death in 415.

Activity period begins with his admission to the Guild of Saint Luke in 1472 and ends with his death in 1519. Republic of Florence is used as his representative polity; later residences belong in place-level data.

role: Member of the Committee of Public Safety and de facto leader
notes: Served as a dominant member of the Committee of Public Safety during the French First Republic from 1793 until his overthrow and execution in 1794.

role: Prince of Wales and rebel leader
notes: Led the Welsh revolt from 1400, proclaimed himself Prince of Wales, and headed a de facto independent Welsh government. His last reliably documented activity dates to 1415.
Served as Lord Protector and exercised supreme executive authority over the Commonwealth of England, Scotland and Ireland from 1653 until his death in 1658.
Reigned as emperor of the Khmer Empire from 928 to 941 and established Koh Ker as the imperial capital.

Reigned as king of the Ayutthaya Kingdom from 1656 until 1688. His reign was marked by extensive international trade and diplomatic relations, especially with France, Persia and European trading powers.
Reigned as king of the Toungoo Empire from 1550 until 1581 and created the largest empire in the history of mainland Southeast Asia.
Reigned as Roman emperor from 117 to 138, consolidated the empire's frontiers, and sponsored major building projects across the Roman world.

role: King of the Arverni and leader of the Gallic Confederation
notes: United many Gallic tribes against Julius Caesar in 52 BCE, won at Gergovia, and surrendered after the Siege of Alesia. Gaul is used as the map-level polity label for the coalition.
Reigned as Mai of the Kanem-Bornu Empire from about 1571 to 1603, reforming its military and administration and presiding over the empire's height.

Traditionally regarded as the founder of the Rurikid dynasty. According to the Primary Chronicle, he began ruling in Novgorod in 862 and ruled until 879; Kievan Rus' is used as the map-level successor polity label.

Traditionally regarded as the first permanent Norse settler of Iceland and the founder of the settlement at Reykjavik around 874. Settlement of Iceland is treated as a distinct map polity before the Icelandic Commonwealth.
Pharaoh of Egypt's Eighteenth Dynasty. Reigned under the birth name Amenhotep IV before adopting the name Akhenaten, promoted the cult of Aten, and founded Akhetaten as a new royal capital.
Ruled Palenque from 615 until 683 and oversaw a major period of political recovery, architectural expansion and dynastic commemoration. Also known as Pakal the Great.
